reason: The cited evidence does not address yttrium behavior, defect sinking by Y, or precipitation in W38Ta36Cr15V11. E1 discusses He migration in the unmodified alloy, and E2 discusses configurational entropy effects in a different HEA system, neither supporting the key premises.
premises: Yttrium segregates to grain boundaries and/or forms finely dispersed Y-rich oxide particles in the alloy
Yttrium at grain boundaries or as particles acts as an effective point defect sink under irradiation
Enhanced defect sinking suppresses radiation-induced precipitation by reducing defect mobility and local supersaturation
The unmodified nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 alloy exhibits radiation-induced precipitation at ~8 dpa
The Y-modified alloy retains negligible irradiation hardening comparable to the unmodified alloy
